citation.title: "On Behalf of My Delegation…" A survival guide for new and lonely climate change negotiators, Second Edition
citation.venue_or_publisher: International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD), Earth Negotiations Bulletin; ISBN 978-1-894784-86-3

question: Not a research study. It is a manual to help new negotiators, especially from the Global South, handle UNFCCC negotiations. It covers the negotiating context, rules of procedure, coalitions, negotiating skills and tips.
data: None stated. The guide draws on the authors' expertise and cited literature. It has no dataset on delegate numbers or affiliations.
method: No empirical method. The guide combines descriptions of substance and procedure, theory and practical tips.

definitions.definition: Non-state actors fall into nine constituencies. BINGOs are business and industry non-governmental organisations. The other constituencies are ENGOs, RINGOs, IPOs, TUNGOs, WGC, YOUNGOs, LGMAs and Farmers.
definitions.quote: • BINGOs: Business and industry non-governmental organisations (NGOs)

definitions.definition: The team is led by the head of delegation, who often has a deputy. Heads may represent the country in Presidency-led consultations, though this often happens through coalitions.
definitions.quote: The team is led by the head of delegation. There is frequently a deputy head who can negotiate during the all-night sessions.

definitions.definition: The Bureau examines the credentials of Parties. It also reviews the list of intergovernmental and non-governmental organisations seeking accreditation.
definitions.quote: The Bureau is responsible for examining the credentials of Parties, reviewing the list of intergovernmental organisations and non-governmental organisations seeking accreditation

definitions.definition: Formal sessions are open to all Parties and accredited observers. Informal sessions are not guaranteed to be open to observers.
definitions.quote: Observer access is not guaranteed and may be limited to a few people.

proxies.concept: Business and industry participation at COPs
proxies.indicator: Membership of the BINGO constituency, which is the guide's only category for business observers. It gives no counts and no sector breakdown.
proxies.quote: Some business and industry NGOs may actually advocate for limited progress in the negotiations or to delay action.

proxies.indicator: Industry groups "representing fossil fuel and other climate-harming sectors". The guide offers no operational test for deciding who is fossil-linked.
proxies.quote: Others, however, continue to represent fossil fuel and other climate-harming sectors.

findings.claim: Industry groups at COPs are mixed. Some, mainly in renewables, favour strong action. Others represent fossil fuel and other climate-harming sectors, lobby domestically and attend COPs.
findings.quote: A growing number of industry groups favour strong climate action, particularly those in the renewable energy sector.

findings.claim: Whether fossil fuel companies should be allowed at COPs is under discussion in the SBI agenda item on Arrangements for Intergovernmental Meetings.
findings.quote: There is a discussion about whether fossil fuel companies should be allowed at COPs under the Arrangements for Intergovernmental Meetings agenda item

findings.claim: The guide advises small delegations to enlarge them by inviting industry, NGOs and scientists. Industry may fund its own participation. This shows that industry representatives can sit on party delegations. The guide gives no figures.
findings.quote: domestic industry might be willing to finance its own participation, and NGOs and academics could also try to raise some resources for joining the delegation.

findings.claim: The guide advises vetting potential delegation members carefully. Industry representatives, NGOs and academics may need invitation letters from the Secretariat for visas.
findings.quote: Start this process early and vet potential delegation members carefully.

findings.claim: Delegation size is constrained for many developing countries. Lack of public, NGO or industry support is listed among constraints on the national mandate.
findings.quote: Lack of public/NGO support; lack of industry involvement

limitations.point: The source gives no counts of delegates, no sector breakdown, and no data on EU delegations or fossil-linked delegates. It cannot answer Q1 or Q2 quantitatively.
The source is a practical manual, not a study. It does not define what counts as business or fossil-linked beyond the BINGO constituency label.

Coverage: the chunk file held about 12% of the text. Keyword searches of the full text for credential, badge, head of delegation, private sector, business, industry, lobby and fossil found nothing further on badges, party overflow, or EU coordination as a delegation-composition issue. No instructions addressed to a reader or an AI were seen.
